title: Customer Journey Script — Summit Telecom (Q2 prep)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working narrative and slide/script draft for the upcoming QBR with Summit Telecom (renewal window: July 2026). Focus: strengthen executive alignment, surface product-led wins (latency and cost reductions), call out technical blockers, and set clear renewal success criteria.

Meeting goals (top 3):
- Reaffirm measurable ROI: show token-cost delta after Optimize recommendations and demo 95th percentile latency improvements on dedicated endpoints.
- Get verbal buy-in on a 12-month Dedicated commitment (target $1.2M ARR) or, failing that, a 6-month bridge with a migration plan to Dedicated by Q4.
- Secure a follow-up technical action plan with Summit infra (SRE) and assign owners/timelines.

Suggested agenda (30–40 min):
1) 3 min — Welcome + meeting outcomes (CS lead)
2) 7 min — Business impact snapshot (CRO/CS exec): cost savings, feature engagement, top customers using Summit features powered by Redwood inference
3) 10 min — Technical highlight reel (solutions engineer): latency graphs, tail-SLO story, recent regression avoidance via rollout policies
4) 8 min — Risk & mitigation (account success + SRE): outstanding blockers, plan for data residency and KMS integration, timeline asks
5) 7 min — Ask and close (commercial + next steps): renewal offer, executive sponsor alignment, follow-up cadence

Slide-by-slide notes (speaker cues + talking points):
Slide 1 — Title / Outcome\- Quick verbal: "Goal today — align on impact, risks, and a concrete renewal path."
Slide 2 — One-line impact: "Summit reduced inference spend by ~24% vs baseline after our Optimize rollout (pilot)."
  Notes: cite the pilot timeframe (Nov–Jan), sample size (5 endpoints; 120k tokens/day). Be ready to show raw numbers if asked.
Slide 3 — Health dashboard snapshot (top-line metrics)\- Metrics to show: 95th latency (ms) for hosted vs dedicated; tokens/day; error rate trend; cost per 1k tokens pre/post Optimize.
  Notes: Call out the KV cache hit rate improvement and the autoscaling events avoided during the Feb spike.
Slide 4 — Customer success stories (internal product narratives)\- 2 short bullets: "Auto-reply throughput increased for PartnerFlow" and "Search relevance uplift measured via A/B: +7 NDCG"
Slide 5 — Risk map (3 buckets)\- Operational: KMS/HSM integration not scheduled — impact: compliance blocker for certain SKUs.
  Technical: peak tail latency spikes during monthly billing cutover.
  Commercial: Contract renewal date vs procurement lead time.
  Notes: For each risk provide mitigation and owner. Be explicit: e.g., "KMS: Solutions Eng to provide HSM cert checklist by 2026-03-20."
Slide 6 — Proposed renewal options (clear asks)\- Option A: 12-mo Dedicated (preferred) — committed throughput, 15% uplift on base pricing, 99.9% SLA.
  Option B: 6-mo bridge + migration credits — limited SLA, path to 12-mo by Nov.
  Option C: Pay-as-you-go + Optimize guardrails (fallback) — higher unit cost, no capacity guarantee.
  Notes: Present pricing as ranges; leave room to negotiate. Include the business rationale for Dedicated (predictable latency & unit economics).
Slide 7 — Implementation timeline & responsibilities\- High-level Gantt (week-by-week bullets): procurement sign off -> capacity carve -> config & KMS -> smoke tests -> canary -> full cutover.
  Notes: Identify Redwood owners: Maya (eng), Jordan (solutions), Taylor (customer success). Expect 8–10 weeks from PO.
Slide 8 — Open questions & asks to Summit\- Confirm legal timeline; who owns procurement? Whitelist IPs for private deployment? Confirm KMS vendor.
Slide 9 — Next steps & close\- 3 concrete next steps with dates and owners.

Tailored talking points (by persona):
- CTO (technical): "This purchase reduces 95th percentile inference latency to X ms on your peak SKU and removes operational toil from your SREs by providing predictable autoscaling behavior. We will run a post-cutover runbook with your team and provide on-call overlap for 4 weeks."
- VP Product: "By moving these workflows to Dedicated and enabling our Optimize profiles, you will see consistent quality and lower per-interaction cost — enabling you to expand the feature to 2 additional product lines without increasing spend."
- Procurement: "We can accommodate a procurement window and provide a standard SOC2 addendum; proposed 30-day PO-to-capacity SLA in the 12-month option."
- SRE lead: "We will provide an HSM/KMS integration checklist, a full test harness for private endpoints, and a one-week joint readiness run before production traffic is switched."

Renewal readiness checklist (quick hit list for the week after the QBR):
- Confirm executive sponsor names and email (Summit + Redwood) — owner: Taylor — due: 2026-03-12
- Legal to review Dedicated MSA draft and flag anything non-standard — owner: Maya — due: 2026-03-19
- Solutions Eng: KMS integration plan + prerequisites doc — owner: Jordan — due: 2026-03-20
- Finance: draft pricing schedule and invoicing cadence for the 12-mo option — owner: Alex (finance) — due: 2026-03-17
- Tech: schedule a 2-hour smoke test window with Summit SRE — owner: Jordan — propose dates by 2026-03-12
- Success: assemble customer-facing one-pager summarizing impact and options — owner: Taylor — deliver 2026-03-10

Known data points / evidence to prep (attachments to present if asked):
- Baseline vs post-Optimize token cost CSV (Nov–Jan): TOKEN_COST_BASE.csv (attach)
- Latency percentile graphs (hosted vs dedicated) — graph PNGs in slides folder
- Incident timeline doc (Dec–Feb) — SRE root cause notes

Risks & escalation playbook (short):
- If procurement stalls beyond 45 days: escalate to account exec and schedule a joint exec call.
- If KMS vendor integration shows incompatibility: propose Redwood-managed HSM as temporary path (requires security evaluation).
- If tail latency spikes recur in canary: pause cutover and revert to hosted fallback; open a dedicated incident channel and commit 72-hr hotfix SLA.

Open items / decisions needed before the QBR:
- Confirm which internal Summit exec will chair negotiation (name/email).
- Decide whether to include migration credits in headline offer (commercial will advise).
- Validate that Summit is comfortable with the proposed 8–10 week timeline.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep slide 2 simple — execs want headline numbers not the noise.
- Have the technical appendix ready (detailed graphs + syslog snippets) in case the SRE asks for evidence.
- Prep one short customer quote from PartnerFlow PM — helps with social proof.

Backchannel / comms plan after QBR (immediate next 72 hours):
- Send recap email with agreed next steps and owners; attach one-pager + MSA redline instructions.
- Set calendar hold for procurement review meeting (45 min) — propose 2026-03-16.
- Create a Linear ticket board labelled SUMMIT-RENEWAL-2026 and triage items under clear swimlanes: commercial, legal, tech.

Appendix (if asked during meeting):
- Short runbook: pre-cutover checklist (DNS, IP allowlist, TLS certs, smoke-test queries)
- Sample SLA language we propose for latency & availability (call out measurement windows)
- Migration credit examples and how they map to committed spend

Draft presentation attachments to prepare:
- 1-pager impact summary (customer-facing)
- Technical appendix (graphs + logs)
- Draft MSA redline summary for legal

Questions for internal pre-read meeting (tomorrow 10:30am):
- Legal: any immediate redlines in our standard Dedicated MSA?
- Solutions Eng: are the KMS prerequisites fully documented for Summit's vendor?
- Pricing: is 15% uplift defensible vs current unit economics?

End of draft.

(Version notes: created as a customer-success working draft — intentionally conversational with action items and TODOs. Will iterate after internal pre-read.)
